name: Toughness
verdict: Coupon (Test_02, no anti-aliasing) at 9.2 s, bottom 18 s x 4, 295 layers. Held well to the plate, every feature printed. Vat 74.6 -> 72.1 g = 2.5 g = 2.16 ml; the dashboard estimate was 2.08 ml (+4 %).
about: SUNLU's tough resin. Made to give a little instead of snapping, so it suits parts that have to be handled.
take: Re-tested in November: strips and coupon confirm 9.2 s at 0.05 mm and 12.4 s at 0.10 mm. Soft and rubbery off the printer, it hardens over a couple of days but keeps a little give - it bends rather than snaps.

tests.txt: Bars 3.7-14.7 s. The two lowest never cured and 6.4 s was still very soft. From 7.8 s the bars formed, and their thickness grew up to 12.4 s (0.27 mm), then stopped. The lowest good bar plus one step gives 9.2 s - the same as the best earlier coupon.
The coupon at 9.2 s, the exposure from the strips. Held well to the plate, and every feature printed.
The same coupon at 0.10 mm. The exposure is the 0.05 one scaled by the ratio used for every resin, 12.4 s, and it printed fine.

Two 14.5 mm lattice cubes at 9.2 s. The one printed on its corner came out symmetric, the upright one with slightly bulging sides. Soft and rubbery off the printer - extra UV changed nothing - they hardened over a couple of days but kept a little give: the 1 mm support pad took about ten bends before it broke.
